one_line: AI funding stalls, policy tightens on data centers, research breakthroughs emerge, and firms roll out new AI products.

themes.title: AI funding and market shifts
themes.text: Anthropic is proceeding with a November IPO targeting a $1.25‑$1.75 trillion valuation, while OpenAI closed an $11 billion funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation. At the same time, Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly 27 % of its workforce, AI spending flatlined in late summer, and Asian tech indexes fell sharply amid AI‑related investor concerns.

stories.headline: Anthropic presses on with November IPO plans despite global AI stock sell-off
OpenAI closes $11 billion in funding at $1.25 trillion valuation
Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as AI spending grows
Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
Asian tech stocks plunge amid fears US Democrats may delay data centers

themes.title: Policy pressure on data centers
themes.text: Voter measures in the 2026 U.S. midterms blocked new data‑center projects and Democrats are preparing tighter oversight of Nvidia’s chip exports and financing. OpenAI announced it will stop using NDAs with public officials and cover full power costs for its data centers. A coalition of tech firms and environmental groups is negotiating a national data‑center framework, while activists breached a Microsoft AI data‑center site in Amsterdam and Meta delayed a policy change that would have allowed AI training on linked sites.

stories.headline: U.S. midterm elections bring voter backlash and new restrictions for AI data centers
OpenAI steps back from NDAs and promises full power costs for data centers
Democrats plan tighter oversight of Nvidia on chip exports and financing
Big tech and environmental groups negotiate national data center framework
Activists breach Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam as protests spread across Europe
Meta pauses commercial terms update that would have allowed AI training on linked sites

themes.title: New AI research milestones
themes.text: Physical Superintelligence’s internal AI system, using a non‑public Anthropic model, produced a machine‑checked proof of the Aaronson‑Ambainis conjecture and released the formalization publicly. OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench, a 100‑task benchmark to evaluate AI agents on wet‑lab data interpretation.

stories.headline: Physical Superintelligence AI system proves Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
OpenAI launches BioBasicsBench to evaluate AI agents on wet‑lab tasks

themes.title: Corporate AI product and hardware moves
themes.text: Airbnb said it will launch a custom AI travel‑agent interface in early 2027. Nvidia required Southeast Asian cloud partners to join a chip‑tracking program to monitor AI chip locations. Google bought roughly 3 million Qualcomm shares for $548 million. Microsoft ended its AI cloud rental from Oracle after older‑generation Nvidia GPUs no longer met its workload needs.

stories.headline: Airbnb announces plans to launch an AI travel agent in 2027
Nvidia requires Southeast Asian cloud partners to enroll in chip‑tracking program
Google spends $548 million to buy about 3 million Qualcomm shares
Microsoft ends Oracle AI cloud rental as older Nvidia GPUs become obsolete
